newsitem.title: USA: Audit criticizes Tennessee local grant program.
newsitem.headline: Audit criticizes Tennessee local grant program.

text.p: A Tennessee comptroller's report urges lawmakers to revamp a program that provides local government grants for water, sewer and road work associated with business development.

The report, released Tuesday, said the Tennessee Industrial Infrastructure Program had become an entitlement program for businesses and lacked adequate oversight to ensure that the companies provided the promised jobs.
It also said the program lacked "a strategic plan" and distributed the grants inequitably among Tennessee's 95 counties.
The program, known as TIIP, was established in 1988 and works closely with a job training pgrogram called the Tennessee Industrial Training Service.

"The General Assembly may wish to consider restructuring the TIIP/ITS program to ensure more accountability," the report said. "Without well-defined accountability mechanisms in place, Tennessee puts itself in a position where companies could misuse the incentives offered."
Gov. Don Sundquist's budget would require local governments to contribute half of the program's proposed $10 million budget for fiscal 1998.
